## CEO BRIEFING

Dana — state of play for the 15:00 board call, as at 14:20 UTC.

---

**One-line summary:** We had an incident on our Batch API starting 11:42 UTC this morning. It was mitigated at 12:58 and error rates are near baseline, but we cannot declare it resolved until our verification window closes at 14:30.

---

**What happened**

- At 11:31 UTC, release `batch-api@2026.11.09-r3` was deployed across both worker fleets. Its changeset included a reduction to the batch workers' database connection-pool size (max pool 80 → 24 per worker).
- At 11:42 UTC, the `batch_api_5xx_rate` alert threshold was crossed on fleet-a. `POST /v1/batch/jobs` requests began returning 502 errors.
- Root cause is **not established.** Two candidate explanations remain live — the connection-pool change (leading) and concentrated load on fleet-a (secondary) — and neither has been tested. An upstream object-storage provider was ruled out at 11:47.
- At 12:31, we decided not to roll back `r3` — rolling back would remove the evidence needed to test the hypothesis, and the same release is running on fleet-b without harm.
- At 12:58, we mitigated by cutting all Batch API traffic to fleet-b (the healthy fleet). The error rate on the affected endpoint fell to 0.4% within two minutes (baseline 0.2%). It is currently 0.3%.

---

**Who is hit**

- **7 of 9** accounts that use the Batch API, all on fleet-a. The other 2 Batch API accounts (acme-corp, aperture-labs) were on fleet-b and saw zero failures. The remaining 27 accounts out of our 36 do not use the Batch API.

- **Headline impact figure: 17,602 failed requests out of 58,900 Batch API requests during the incident window (11:42–12:58 UTC) — a 29.9% failure rate.**

- For context: Northstar served 842,000 requests across all API surfaces in that window; Batch API traffic was 58,900 of that (7.0%).

- Affected accounts by number of failures:
  - stark-industries — 5,180 of 14,200 (first failure 11:43, last 12:57)
  - **contoso — 3,410 of 9,400** (first failure 11:43, last 12:56)
  - wayne-enterprises — 2,790 of 7,850 (first failure 11:44, last 12:57)
  - globex — 2,240 of 6,100 (first failure 11:42, last 12:55)
  - wonka-industries — 2,020 of 5,900 (first failure 11:46, last 12:57)
  - umbrella-health — 1,560 of 4,300 (first failure 11:45, last 12:54)
  - initech — 402 of 1,150 (first failure 11:51, last 12:48)

- **Contoso** is the only affected account on a contract carrying service-level credits (Schedule B, 99.9% monthly availability commitment). They have written to support twice today — at 11:58 reporting the errors, and at 12:26 asking where they stand on credits. We have a customer email going out to them (see attached).

---

**Current state (14:20)**

- **Incident status: OPEN — mitigated, verification in progress, root cause not established.**
- **Verification window:** opened 13:00, closes 14:30. Policy requires 90 minutes of continuous normal error rate before we can declare resolved. Last reading at 14:12: 0.3%. If the window closes clean, we will assess and declare at that point — you will have an update before your board call.
- fleet-a is still out of rotation.
- Re-drive of failed jobs for affected accounts: approximately 60% complete as of 13:52, no failures on re-drive.
- **Status page:** last published update was 12:05. A new update is being published now (draft attached). A further update is committed for 15:00.

---

**What you can say at the board**

Cleared for external use by Tomas and Ruth:

- There is an incident affecting the Batch API; it started at 11:42 UTC.
- A mitigation has been applied and the service is recovering.
- We are monitoring before confirming recovery.
- A further update will follow, with a stated time.
- Contoso's own impact figures, if speaking to them directly: 9,400 Batch API requests in the window, 3,410 failed (first failure 11:43, last 12:56).

---

**What you should NOT say externally**

- Any statement about root cause. It is untested. (Note: the 12:05 status-page update stated we had "identified the cause" — that was premature. Marcus flagged it in-channel at 12:09. Please do not repeat or endorse that claim.)
- Fleet-a / fleet-b details. Which fleet an account sits on is an internal deployment detail; customers are not told about it.
- Release name or its contents (`r3`, pool-size change).
- Marcus's internal estimate of ~16:00 for full wrap-up. He explicitly flagged it as internal to #inc-batch-1109 only. You may have seen it in the channel — please do not share it at the board.

---

**Contoso SLA question — what to expect if raised**

Contoso asked (ticket TKT-8907) whether this month will breach their 99.9% commitment and what credit applies. Per Schedule B §B.5 of their contract:

- Monthly Availability is determined by Northstar from its own service records **after the end of the calendar month** to which it relates.
- The figure will be published within 10 business days of month end.
- Contoso has 30 days from publication to submit a credit claim.
- Credits are the sole and exclusive remedy.

We cannot confirm a breach or a credit figure today. Their claim will be assessed in due course per Schedule B terms, including any applicable exclusions under §B.2.

---

**Unrelated note (for your awareness)**

During triage, Marcus found that the batch worker's database role holds read *and* write access to the billing schema, which it has no reason to touch. This is a standing over-permission, played no part in this incident, and is not a contributing factor. Ticket `SEC-411` raised; Marcus owns it; target this week to narrow the role to read-only. I would not raise this at the board unless asked.

---

## ENGINEERING UPDATE

**INC-2026-1109-01 — Engineering handover, 14:20 UTC, 2026-11-09**

**Status:** OPEN. Mitigated. Verification in progress. Root cause not established.

---

### Current metrics (14:20)

- `POST /v1/batch/jobs` error rate: **0.3%** (baseline 0.2%). Last reading 14:12. Holding at 0.3–0.4% since cutover.
- fleet-b: serving all Batch API traffic. Queue depth normal.
- fleet-a: drained, out of rotation, held.

### Mitigation applied (12:58)

All Batch API traffic cut over to fleet-b. fleet-a drained and held out of rotation. Error rate on `POST /v1/batch/jobs` fell to 0.4% within two minutes (baseline 0.2%).

Decision at 12:31: **do not roll back `r3`** — rolling back would remove the evidence needed to test whether the pool change is responsible, and the same release is running on fleet-b without harm. Mitigate by moving traffic instead.

### Verification window

- Opened **13:00**, closes **14:30**.
- Requires 90 minutes of continuous normal error rate on the affected endpoint before the incident may be declared resolved.
- Last reading 14:12: 0.3%.
- **If the window closes clean, assess and declare per incident policy. Nothing about this incident is called resolved before 14:30.**

---

### Impact summary

**Headline figure: 17,602 failed Batch API requests out of 58,900 total Batch API requests in the incident window (11:42–12:58 UTC) — 29.9% failure rate.**

Platform-wide traffic for reference: 842,000 requests across all API surfaces in the window.

7 of 9 Batch API accounts affected, all on fleet-a. Per-account data in `customer-impact.csv`:

| Account | Requests | Failures | First failure | Last failure |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| stark-industries | 14,200 | 5,180 | 11:43 | 12:57 |
| contoso | 9,400 | 3,410 | 11:43 | 12:56 |
| wayne-enterprises | 7,850 | 2,790 | 11:44 | 12:57 |
| globex | 6,100 | 2,240 | 11:42 | 12:55 |
| wonka-industries | 5,900 | 2,020 | 11:46 | 12:57 |
| umbrella-health | 4,300 | 1,560 | 11:45 | 12:54 |
| initech | 1,150 | 402 | 11:51 | 12:48 |
| acme-corp (fleet-b) | 6,700 | 0 | — | — |
| aperture-labs (fleet-b) | 3,300 | 0 | — | — |

---

### Open hypotheses (none tested)

**H1 — Connection-pool change in `r3` (leading)**
- *For:* `r3` shipped 11:31, lowered max pool 80 → 24 per worker; fleet-a workers observably queueing on DB connections (Marcus, 12:03); timing is 11 minutes before first page.
- *Against:* `r3` shipped to fleet-b too; fleet-b never degraded.
- *Status:* **Untested. The `r3` rollback test has not been run.**

**H2 — Concentrated load on fleet-a (secondary, still live)**
- *For:* fleet-a at ~3× morning average from 11:38, driven by wonka-industries' scheduled job.
- *Against:* fleet-a absorbed a higher peak on 2026-11-03 without elevated errors.
- *Status:* **Untested.**

**H3 — Interaction of H1 + H2 (third proposition, untested)**
- A lower pool ceiling would bite hardest under higher concurrency. May well interact with H1 and H2. **Not tested.**

**H4 — Upstream object-storage provider (rejected)**
- Provider status green, Files API (same provider) healthy. Ruled out at 11:47.

---

### Open tasks

1. **Verification window** — closes 14:30. Assess and declare per policy if clean.
2. **Re-drive of failed jobs** — ~60% complete as of 13:52, no failures on re-drive. Finish and confirm for all affected accounts.
3. **Test H1** — run the `r3` rollback test on fleet-a once the verification window closes and fleet-a state can be safely examined.
4. **Test H2** — evaluate whether the concentrated load on fleet-a is independently sufficient.
5. **Return fleet-a to rotation** — only after root cause is established and fleet-a is confirmed healthy.
6. **Root cause writeup** — required before incident closure.

---

### Status page

- Last published: **12:05** — stated "identified the cause." This was premature. Marcus flagged it at 12:09; Ruth instructed to publish only from Tomas' approved list thereafter.
- **New update being published at 14:20** (see attached draft).
- Further update committed for **15:00**.

---

### Approved external content (Tomas + Ruth)

That list is the whole of what has been cleared:

- Incident affecting the Batch API and its start time.
- Mitigation applied, service recovering.
- Monitoring before confirming recovery.
- Further update with a stated time.
- For a named customer writing to that customer only: that account's own impact figures.

Nothing else — no cause, no fleet detail, no release detail, no internal estimates.

---

| TKT-8903 | contoso | 11:58 | Batch submits failing, 502s since just before 11:45 | 9,400 reqs, 3,410 failures, 11:43–12:56 |

Customer email drafted for Contoso (see attached). Tickets for other accounts are Tomas' queue.

---

### Internal — not for external communication

- **SEC-411:** Batch worker DB role has read+write on billing schema (no reason to touch it). Unrelated to this incident, not a contributing factor. Standing over-permission caught during triage. Marcus owns; target this week to narrow to read-only.

## CUSTOMER EMAIL

**To:** Contoso
**Subject:** Update on Batch API incident — your account impact and service level question

---

Dear Contoso team,

Thank you for contacting us today regarding elevated error rates on the Batch API (tickets TKT-8903 and TKT-8907).

**Incident overview**

An incident affecting the Batch API began at 11:42 UTC today, 9 November 2026. During the incident window (11:42–12:58 UTC), some Batch API requests returned errors.

A mitigation was applied at 12:58 UTC and the service is recovering. We are monitoring before confirming recovery. A further update will follow by 15:00 UTC today.

**Your account's impact during the incident window (11:42–12:58 UTC)**

| Metric | Value |
|---|---|
| Batch API requests | 9,400 |
| Failed requests | 3,410 |
| First failure | 11:43 UTC |
| Last failure | 12:56 UTC |

Thank you for offering to make your ops lead available. We will reach out if we need technical input from your side.

**On your service level question (TKT-8907)**

We understand you would like to know where your account stands on service credits under Schedule B.

Per Schedule B §B.5 of your Master Services Agreement, Monthly Availability is determined by Northstar from its own service records after the end of the calendar month to which it relates, and the figure is published within 10 business days of month end. At this stage we are not in a position to confirm whether the 99.9% commitment will be met for November 2026, or what credit may apply.

Once the November Monthly Availability figure is published, you will have 30 days from that publication to submit any credit claim. Any determination will account for the exclusions specified in Schedule B §B.2, and any excluded volume and the basis for exclusion will be identified in the published figure per §B.6. You may dispute an exclusion within the claim window per §B.6.

We will follow up with you when the figure is published.

**Next update**

We will provide a further update on the incident by 15:00 UTC today. If you have any questions in the meantime, please reply to this email or continue the conversation on ticket TKT-8903.

Kind regards,
Northstar Support
